principles.name: Bureaucratic friction
principles.rule: Hidden power is divided by forms, budgets, approvals, staffing, maintenance, and turf wars.

principles.name: Budget test
principles.rule: Every conspiracy consumes labor, facilities, supply chains, data storage, training, and political capital.

principles.name: Jurisdiction test
principles.rule: Secret offices overlap, contradict, and sometimes sabotage one another because no one has universal authority.

principles.name: Succession test
principles.rule: A hidden system must explain who inherits command keys, memories, liabilities, and legitimacy.

principles.name: Procurement test
principles.rule: Impossible technology still needs materials, contractors, test failures, repair, and disposal.

principles.name: Error budget
principles.rule: Coverups fail through ordinary mistakes, personality conflicts, and poorly specified objectives.

principles.name: Partial truth
principles.rule: A false public story may protect a real but different program; the true part should not authenticate the false whole.

principles.name: Human motive
principles.rule: Characters need love, fear, status, guilt, ideology, grief, or ambition beyond faction doctrine.

principles.name: One-percent-better rule
principles.rule: A vast institution is believable when it improves outcomes marginally, not when it flawlessly controls everything.

principles.name: Comedy boundary
principles.rule: Satire can remix harmless or fictional motifs, but must not launder scapegoating or dehumanizing conspiracy claims into canon.
